title: Muthoot Finance and CDSL Q2 FY27 Performance
summary: Muthoot Finance reported a 36% profit rise to ₹3,278 crore, driven by gold loan growth, while CDSL saw a 24% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to ₹173 crore. Both companies benefited from increased market participation and growth in the Indian securities market.

facts.statement: Muthoot Finance reported a 36% profit rise to ₹3,278 crore in Q2 FY27, driven by gold loan growth.
CDSL reported a 24% year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to ₹173 crore, aided by increased market participation.
Muthoot Finance's standalone profit increased by 27% year-on-year, while CDSL's standalone profit increased by 28% year-on-year.

sources.title: Muthoot Finance Q2 profit rises 27% to ₹2,977 crore, income up 37%
sources.description:
Muthoot Finance on Saturday reported a 27 per cent growth in standalone profit at Rs 2,977 crore in the September quarter.
The company had a profit of Rs 2,345 crore in the July-September quarter of FY26.
Total income rose to Rs 8,842 crore in the July-September quarter, from Rs 6,442 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago, Muthoot Finance said in a regulatory filing.
Interest income rose to Rs 8,730 crore in Q2 of FY27, from Rs 6,304 crore in Q2 of FY26.
For the first half (April-September) of current fiscal year, profit after tax grew 39 per cent to Rs 6,103 crore on a consolidated basis.
Consolidated loan AUM during April-September increased 42 per cent to Rs 2.09 lakh crore.
Consolidated gold loan AUM increased 46 per cent year-on-year to over Rs 1.93 lakh crore.

sources.title: CDSL Q2 profit rises 24% to ₹173 cr as demat accounts grow by 7.5 million
sources.description:
Central Depository Services (India) Ltd (CDSL) reported a 24 per cent year-on-year rise in consolidated net profit to Rs 173 crore for the July-September quarter, aided by continued growth in India's securities market participation.
Consolidated total income rose 22 per cent to Rs 417 crore in the second quarter of FY27, compared with Rs 341 crore a year earlier. Sequentially, net profit jumped 47 per cent from Rs 118 crore in the June quarter, while total income increased 22 per cent from Rs 341 crore.
For the first half of FY27, consolidated net profit grew 20 per cent to Rs 291 crore, while total income rose 19 per cent to Rs 758 crore.
On a standalone basis, CDSL's net profit increased 28 per cent year-on-year to Rs 163 crore in Q2, while total income rose 24 per cent to Rs 359 crore. For the six months ended September, standalone profit grew 10 per cent to Rs 308 crore and income increased 14 per cent to Rs 685 crore.

sources.title: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Q2 profit more than doubles to ₹53 crore
sources.description:
Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd (ABFRL) on Saturday reported a twofold increase in consolidated net profit at Rs 53.05 crore for September quarter FY27.
The company had posted a net profit of Rs 23.44 crore during July-September FY26, according to a regulatory filing from ABFRL.
Revenue from operations rose to Rs 2,265.61 crore from Rs 2,037.90 crore earlier.
Total expenses of ABFRL, which handles Pantaloons and Style Up, along with a host of ethnic brands, were at Rs 2,224.99 crore, up 9.71 per cent in the second quarter of FY27.
Total income, including other income, was up 11.48 per cent to Rs 2,295.42 crore in Q2 FY27.
Last year, the Aditya Birla Group demerged its Madura business into a separately listed entity, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL), effective from May 1, 2025.

sources.title: IGL Q2 result: Net profit plunges 93.5% to ₹24 crore on higher gas costs
sources.description:
Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL), the country's largest city gas distributor, reported a sharp 93.5 per cent decline in standalone net profit for the September quarter as a substantial increase in input gas costs eroded margins, offsetting higher sales volumes and revenue.
Net profit fell to Rs 24.38 crore in the second quarter of 2026-27 from Rs 372.51 crore a year earlier, despite an 8 per cent increase in sales volumes and a 26 per cent jump in gross turnover.
The company said its average daily gas sales crossed the 10 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) mark for the first time, rising to 10.06 mmscmd in the July-September period from 9.31 mmscmd in the corresponding period last year.
Gross sales turnover increased to Rs 5,999.13 crore from Rs 4,431.63 crore, reflecting higher sales as well as the impact of increased gas prices.
